chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, who said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Aban, from one whom he mentioned, attributing it to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him).
He was asked: Is it permissible to say that Allah is a thing? He said: Yes, it removes it from the two limits: the limit of negation (of attributes/existence) and the limit of anthropomorphism.
ai.seo_question: Is it correct to say God is a 'thing' in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In this foundational hadith from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) validates the term 'Shay' (Thing/Entity) as a theological necessity to affirm Allah's objective reality, thereby avoiding the extremes of *Ta'til* (negation of existence) and *Tashbih* (anthropomorphism). This position is central to the Shia doctrine of *Tawhid al-Sifat*, distinguishing between the essence of God and His attributes while maintaining that He is a distinct, existing entity without being confined by physical boundaries.
